_note: Record is the Health Passport. Its §26 paths keep their names and are mounted under /v1/record by reference; the P0 service answers most of them already, in development, on synthetic data, on loopback. Share links and export are proposed; the HL7 v2 inbound path is a supplier's, so it is a door to add rather than a route. Every read goes through the consent gateway.
_encounterStatusesNote: The resource is encounter-statuses and not encounters. A field ending Ref is read as a reference into the store of the engine that declares its resource, so declaring encounters here would make every frozen encounterRef on Care's and Clinical's routes a reach into the record's store, which they are not: they carry the reference and the entry stays in the record.

doorsToAdd.why: ADT, ORU and ORM messages from partner systems are supplier callbacks. §26 names the path /hl7v2/inbound; it is mounted as a door with mutual TLS per partner, not answered as a route.

A claim's diagnosis coding is assembled inside the record and clinical boundary from the signed encounter and handed to the switching partner through this door. Money records the billing side and never holds the coding.

routes.summary: Say whether an encounter is written, signed or superseded, and nothing it contains, to the Care engine deciding whether a visit may be handed over or completed.

request.why: The encounter entry passport.entry.written named, which the nurse hands over and completes against.

response.why: written, signed or superseded. Written is an entry nobody has signed; superseded is one a later entry replaced, and a visit is never completed against it.
When it was signed, present only when it is signed.
The entry that replaced it, present only when it is superseded, so Care can ask about that one instead.

refusals.statement: There is no encounter by that reference here.
refusals.why: An unknown reference and one for an entry of another kind are one answer, so a status request cannot be used to find out what else a patient's record holds.

refusals.statement: That encounter has not been written yet, so it has no status to give.
refusals.why: passport.entry.written is what tells Care an encounter exists. A status asked for before it is heard is a guess at a reference, answered as one.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: It changes nothing and returns no clinical content — a state, a time and a reference — so there is no read of the record's content to emit passport.access.read for. The record keeps its own log of the call.
